about: Steps an agent follows before a resume, CV, cover letter or written answer is considered ready for the candidate to submit.
steps: Start from the brief (`node app/cli.mjs op run brief.get --input '{"applicationId":"ID"}'`). Apply active writing rules within their scope, and start from the suggested narrative and saved bullets.
Re-open the live employer posting and record when it was checked. Note the deadline, required fields and word limits, or say they were not inspected.
Save a qualification-to-evidence map on the job (`qualificationMap`) and list the gaps.
Use what the candidate put in without asking them to confirm it. Ask only about a missing fact this application needs, all in one message, and save the answers.

Cut to what answers the posting: each accomplishment once, about 18 to 24 bullets and 750 to 900 words on two pages. Generate the document from the format files in '3 Templates'. Name the evidence behind each role, and fix what `bulletNotes` points out.

Run an independent review pass (a second agent or a fresh read) clause by clause, for overstatement and understatement: factual scope, qualifiers, attribution, chronology, fit and layout. Apply optional suggestions only if they add no claim.
Export the PDF and look at every page: clipping, overlaps, missing characters, a heading stranded at the bottom of a page, role/date collisions, page count.

Check text and structure: no {{placeholders}} left, no claims carried over from an example, `docs.check` with the material id shows `matchesSaved`, fonts as set in the format file, contact details, dates and figures identical across documents, word count within limits.
Save the result as a new material version in the career library. Earlier versions are never overwritten.

Give it to the candidate for a final read, with gaps and left-out conflicts in the same message. Save good bullets with `bullets.save` and any correction that should last with `rules.save`. Submission then follows their saved submission mode (see app/skills/submit-application.md); afterwards record exactly what was filed, including every question and answer, with the `submissions.record` operation.
